title: Agentrys has raised $24.5M to build the future of chip design.
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni

Mark H. Ren
• 1st
Founder & CEO, Agentrys | Pioneering Agentic Design Automation | Former NVIDIA Research Director | IEEE Fellow

Today, I’m excited to share that Agentrys has raised $24.5M to build the future of chip design.

Chip design is an ideal frontier for self-improving AI. Every design task produces measurable results. Those results can be evaluated by rigorous engineering tools—and those evaluation signals can be used to systematically improve the agents themselves.

Self-improving agents need more than orchestration around traditional tools. They need agent-native tools: tools that expose the right design state, enable precise actions, provide fast and reliable feedback, and make outcomes easy to evaluate.

They also need models that can adapt to specific design domains, workflows, and customer environments. Evaluation signals from real engineering workflows can guide the specialization of these models for the tasks that matter most—creating another level of continuous improvement.

Together, self-improving agents, agent-native tools, and custom models create a closed learning loop—where agents learn from outcomes, models become increasingly specialized, and the entire system continuously improves.

We call this Agentic Design Automation (ADA).

We’re applying ADA to long, complex engineering workflows across chip design—including RTL design, verification, physical design, and analog design—where agents can operate over many steps, interact with engineering tools, learn from rigorous feedback, and improve over time.

Our long-term vision is to help every chip design team build its own ADA system—integrated with its proprietary workflows, tools, data, and design environment, learning from every design task and continuously improving to help engineers tackle increasingly complex design challenges.

This funding will help us expand our team, build more agent-native tools, advance custom models for chip design, and deploy ADA across more customer workflows and more of the chip design flow.

I’m incredibly grateful to Etna Labs, MediaTek , our investors, customers, partners, and especially the Agentrys team for believing in this vision.

We’re just getting started.
